sections.html:
Southwest Iowa's Cass County is about 565 square miles, with Atlantic as the county seat. Atlantic had 6,792 residents in 2020, far more than Griswold (994) or Anita (963). The county overall counted 13,127 people in 2020 and was estimated at 12,960 in 2025, with median home value around $150,300 and 71.6 percent of homes owner-occupied.

Buyers and sellers in the small towns and on rural parcels deal with the same courthouse offices as buyers in Atlantic. Rural parcels, though, carry an extra rural services levy, described below, so check which side of the city line your parcel falls on.

One building, the courthouse at 5 West 7th Street, Atlantic, IA 50022, holds every county office you will need.

  • Treasurer: 712-243-5503. The tax counter opens at 8:00 and closes at 4:30, and a yellow drop box stands outside. Pay online through iowatreasurers.org. Senior and disabled property tax credit claims also run through this office.
  • Assessor: 712-243-2005, weekdays, starting an hour earlier at 7:00 a.m. and finishing at 4:30 p.m. Forms and petitions can be sent to assessors@casscoia.us.
  • Auditor: works out the levy and issues the tax bill.
  • Board of Review: three or five people who work apart from the assessor and may leave a value alone, raise it or cut it.

The assessor sets a house at full market value as of January 1 and redoes real property in odd-numbered years only. Three tools produce the number: recent comparable sales, what it would cost to rebuild less depreciation with the land added, and an income calculation for rentals.

Farmland is judged by what it can produce rather than by sale prices. A building under construction is valued as it stood on New Year's Day.

Setting rates and calculating the tax belong to other offices. What a home owes depends on its value compared with all the value in its taxing district.

The county's levy notice for the fiscal year starting July 1, 2026 lists these rates. Iowa levies are usually stated per $1,000 of taxable value.

Cass County levy rates, current and proposed

Countywide3.857574.78630
Rural additional4.600003.78000
Rural total8.457578.56630

Taxable value for general services grew from 1,187,705,773 to 1,220,800,486. City, school and other levies are added on top for your taxing district. The treasurer can quote the final total for any parcel.

sections.h2: When your Cass County bill is due
sections.html:
Fall half: due September 1, late from October 1. Spring half: due March 1, late from April 1.

Late interest runs 1.5 percent monthly in whole dollars, never under $1. A delinquent notice reaches unpaid owners as of February 1, and April brings a Delinquent Tax Statement and Tax Sale Notice. Balances still open on May 1 pick up a publication fee and get advertised for the June sale.

The postmark must fall on or before the due date. A parcel number is enough to pay if the statement never showed up, and a partial payment is taken so long as it covers the interest and costs.

The auction is set for 8:00 a.m. on the third Monday of June. Adjourned sessions follow on the third Monday of later months. A parcel advertised twice without a buyer moves to a Public Bidder Sale, and the county must buy it if no private bidder steps up.

To redeem, you pay 2 percent for each month since the sale, in guaranteed funds. After the county receives a Certificate of Purchase, the treasurer may also sue in the usual way to collect.

Once taxes are sold, Iowa counts them as paid and attaches a lien to the property. Redemption that never comes lets the certificate holder start deed proceedings, which is why owners behind on taxes should move early.

Written protests go to the Board of Review in spring, April 2 through April 30 (Iowa Code 441.37). Leftover disputes move to district court. Grounds can be equity with similar property, value, classification, errors or fraud.

In odd-numbered years a separate protest period opens for owners hit by a state equalization order. The assessor can give you those dates.

Homestead credit and military exemption claims are accepted all year. Before July 1 they count for the current year, and after July 1 they roll to the next.

Usually the seller's portion of this year's tax is prorated and handed to the buyer as a credit, visible on the closing statement.

Transfer tax runs 80 cents per $500 beyond the first $500, with a declaration of value filed alongside the deed and kept by the assessor for three years. City sewer or water charges certified to the treasurer become liens equal to tax. A mobile home needs a tax clearance form before anyone moves it.

If you will live outside Iowa after the sale, ask whether Iowa income tax could apply to your gain before you close.

sections.h2: Selling a house with unpaid taxes
sections.html: An open balance is just one more line on the settlement statement, and plenty of owners never expect that. Phone the treasurer and ask what each half costs today. Ask also whether your parcel went to the June auction, because if it did the redemption total climbs 2 percent every month, and a faster closing is cheaper. The title company pays the treasurer from your proceeds, and the lien is released when the account is settled. Selling to a cash buyer as-is changes none of that, though it removes repair requests from your timeline.

sections.h2: Which parcels carry the rural services levy
sections.html:
The extra rural levy applies outside the cities, so a farmstead or an acreage near Griswold or Anita pays it while a house in town does not. The table above shows the rural additional rate dropping from 4.60000 to a proposed 3.78000, while the countywide rate rises. The two nearly offset, and the rural total moves from 8.45757 to a proposed 8.56630. A buyer comparing a town house with a country house should ask for the final rate on each parcel instead of relying on these county pieces alone, since the county share is only one part of the whole bill.

It also helps to know which jurisdictions touch your parcel before you list, and a quick call to the treasurer usually settles it. School, city and township levies differ from one place to the next, and the treasurer's office can tell you which apply from the parcel number.

faqs.q: What is the Cass County property tax due date?
faqs.a: The fall half comes due September 1 and the spring half March 1. Penalty interest of 1.5 percent a month follows on October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Where is the Cass County Treasurer?
faqs.a: In the Cass County Courthouse, 5 West 7th Street, Atlantic. Call 712-243-5503, and the property tax counter is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: When does Cass County hold its tax sale?
faqs.a: The third Monday in June at 8:00 a.m., with adjourned sales monthly afterward. Notices must be mailed by May 1.

faqs.q: How often does Cass County reassess property?
faqs.a: Every two years, in odd-numbered years, effective January 1. Homes are valued at 100 percent of market value.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cass County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid taxes and interest come out of the sale proceeds at closing. If the taxes were already sold, the redemption amount, growing at 2 percent a month, is part of the payoff.
